thread:
incident-bot: Pager: GPU queue growth detected for cluster-prod-gpu. queue_length=423, throttled_requests=187, approx 9m sustained growth. threshold=100. Severity: P1. Paging oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: Picking this up. Any immediate customer impact?

incident-bot: Alert enrichment: pods_pending=102, unschedulable_pods=78, reason=1/50 nodes available, node_selector_mismatch observed. Autoscaler events: 3x scale-up blocked. ASG error: LaunchTemplateVersionMismatch. IAM error found in last attach attempt.

alex: Seeing huge queue on the inference ingress. Error spike from downstream batcher: \`k8s-scheduler: "0/50 nodes are available: 50 node(s) didn't match node selector."\`

priya: Running `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep Pending | wc -l` shows 102 indeed. Pulling events.

jamie: I'm on infra. Checking ASG/launch templates now. Likely the new LT has different instance profile so instances can't join the nodegroup properly.

priya: Events snippet: 
```
0/78 nodes are available: 78 node(s) didn't match taint/selector.
Warning  FailedScheduling  2m (x120 over 9m)  default-scheduler  0/78 nodes are available: 78 taint {dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule}
```

taylor: So autoscaler requested nodes but ASG returned instances that were tainted differently, and kubelet didn't register? Can we see EC2 instance logs?

marta: I can see last ASG scale activity: 3 attach attempts at 22:12, 22:14, 22:16. Each time the attach succeeded but userdata failed: cloud-init error when applying kubelet tags -> node came up with taint `dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule` and label `gpu=false`. Autoscaler considered them incompatible with GPU pod node selectors.

chelsea: That's consistent: launch template change last night removed the GPU label step in the bootstrap. CC @ops who deployed the LT change.

alex: Customer impact: several paying customers' realtime endpoints degraded to 1-2 RPS, requests queued. We should start customer comms. Priya can you confirm which customers impacted? We need a quick impact blurb.

priya: Quick list from telemetry: prod-customer-a, prod-customer-c, prod-customer-d. Estimated 12 total deployments affected. Latency 95p jumped from 120ms to 3.6s, error rate +7%. I'll paste dashboard link: https://console.redwood/infra/alerts/2234567890

jamie: Mitigation plan: 1) Manual provision temporary GPU instances into a separate nodegroup with correct LT and proper labels. 2) Roll back LT change if safe, or patch userdata to apply labels. 3) Tolerations? We should avoid changing cluster-wide taints for safety. 4) If we can't provision quick, fallback to CPU pool for non-realtime jobs.

taylor: I'll try a manual ASG scale-up to bring up nodes using the previous LT version. Running: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name prod-gpu-group --desired-capacity 60`

marta: Hold on, the ASG has a max capacity of 50. Current desired=45. Need to increase max first. 

taylor: Increasing max to 80 now. `aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name prod-gpu-group --max-size 80`

incident-bot: Deploy bot triggered: `deploy-bot: launch-template rollback job queued by @jamie`.

jamie: I'm starting a rollback of the LT diff. If rollback fails or is risky, we'll create a new nodegroup and bootstrap script that enforces labels and removes the wrong taint.

chelsea: Heads-up: rollback will kick off node replacements which might temporarily reduce capacity further. We need to be careful.

leo: Can we instead attach a toleration to the inference pods to accept the current taint until nodes have correct labels? Pros: quick. Cons: could place pods onto nodes without GPUs if labels remain missing. Need to ensure node has GPU attached.

priya: We can add toleration + nodeAffinity for `beta.kubernetes.io/instance-type` GPU families as a stopgap. But editing a bunch of deployments is noisy. Maybe a patch to the admission webhook? Not ideal for P1.

oncall-sre: I'm going to open a quick runbook step: 1) patch ASG max, 2) scale ASG to 70, 3) monitor node readiness, 4) if nodes come up with wrong labels, run a bootstrap fix via SSM to set `gpu=true` label and remove incorrect taint. 5) Notify customers.

marta: SSM remediation script prepared: 
```
#!/bin/bash
kubectl label node $NODE_NAME gpu=true --overwrite
kubectl taint nodes $NODE_NAME dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule- || true
systemctl restart kubelet
```
I'll run it once new instances are in EC2 and visible in cluster.

taylor: ASG scaled. New instances launching. EC2 IDs: i-0a1b2c..., i-0d2e3f...  Coming up in 2m.

incident-bot: Alert update: queue_length now 289 (was 423). throttled=90. Pod pending=48. Progress.

alex: Good. Start drafting a short customer message for impacted tenants: mention degraded latency, we have a mitigation in progress, ETA 30-60m, ticket created. @marta can you add precise ETA when nodes are ready?

marta: ETA ~22:40 for nodes to join and be remediated.

jamie: Rollback in progress completed for LT. It replaced the faulty bootstrap. New nodes should now come up with correct labels automatically. We will still run SSM for the 6 nodes that previously came up wrong.

leo: Running an admission webhook patch is more invasive; hold off. SSM labeling is safer for this window.

chelsea: Ops note: we should also audit the CI pipeline that published the LT change. I saw a commit that touched cloud-init templates. Marking follow-up task.

priya: Customer comms draft: 
"We're investigating increased latency on GPU inference endpoints. We're provisioning additional GPU capacity and expect normal service within ~30-60 minutes. We'll update with progress and a root cause timeline after mitigation."

alex: Send now and include link to status page and support contact.

incident-bot: Customer notification sent by @alex. Message ID 789123.

marta: Running SSM remediation on nodes listed. First 3 patched, labels applied. Nodes rejoin as `gpu=true`. Pods starting to schedule.

incident-bot: Update: queue_length 67, throttled_requests 12, pending_pods 8.

oncall-sre: Monitoring logs: no further autoscaler blocks. Scale-up events now healthy. ASG is stable at 70 desired, 68 InService.

priya: Telemetry confirms impacted customers' endpoints recovering. Latency trending back to baseline. I'm capturing metrics for postmortem.

alex: Good job team. Post-incident actions: 1) Postmortem with timeline, 2) fix CI to require LT bootstrap tests, 3) add autoscaler health-check guard to avoid scale attempts when LT mismatch detected, 4) run a dry-run of SSM labeling in staging.

jamie: Opening incident doc: https://docs.redwood/incidents/2234567890 (I'll fill timeline).

chelsea: I'll own the CI fix.

leo: I'll add an autoscaler blocker detection rule.

marta: I'll add the SSM remediation playbook to run automatically the next time node joins with missing labels.

incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged, mitigation successful, moving to stabilization state.

alex: Closing the pager after 2h of monitoring post-mitigation. Final impact: 12 customers briefly degraded, no data loss, duration ~1h20m for full recovery. Postmortem owners assigned.

priya: Copying metrics and dashboards into the incident doc.

oncall-sre: If anything regresses, reopen. Otherwise moving to retrospective. :thumbsup:
